message_1_subject: Post-demo: response robustness playbook & decode-resilience next steps
message_1_body:
Hi Morgan / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo time this morning — really appreciated the product context and the examples you shared for your transaction-categorization pipeline. I created a short ‘robustness playbook’ draft (attached) that maps our recommended JSON-safety patterns to the specific risks you flagged. High-level items we covered: 

• Schema hardening: single canonical schema + narrow enums for critical fields
• Constrained decoding: soft token penalties + top-k constraints during generation
• Runtime validation: lightweight JSON validator with fast failure modes and a retry policy for transient decode failures
• Embeddings + reranker flow: deterministic candidate IDs + fallback to cached embeddings for cold start

Action items I propose next:
1) Technical deep-dive with Dev (30–45m) to walk the SDK hooks for validation and retry (Dev will lead).
2) Share a min schema subset you absolutely need (3 fields) so we can prototype the constrained decoder behavior on a sample prompt.
3) Decide fail-open vs fail-closed behavior for your UI (we recommend fail-open with scored warning for non-critical fields).

I’ve attached the playbook and a JSON schema proposal (finlytics-schema-proposal-v2.json). Dev — can you take point on a short call Tuesday to go over SDK integration and the token-level validation hooks?

Thanks,
— Soojin
Soojin Lee

message_3_subject: Re: Post-demo: response robustness playbook & decode-resilience next steps — proposed patterns
message_3_body:
Hi Morgan / Priya — looping in quick technical patterns we can run in a short proof-of-concept: 

Pattern A — Strict whitelist + fallback (Fail-closed primary):
• Constrained decoder uses a token-level whitelist derived from the schema enum.
• If output violates schema, immediately return an error and trigger a synchronous fallback: re-run generation with stronger constraints or call a lightweight deterministic reranker.
• Pros: deterministic, minimal downstream validation. Cons: higher latency on first request when whitelist triggers fallbacks.

Pattern B — Soft-validate + retry-with-temperature (Fail-open primary):
• Generate with a mild top-k/top-p constraint. Run validator; if non-critical fields fail, return output but mark warning and schedule an immediate async retry with lower temperature and a decoding constraint.
• For critical fields, block the response and perform a synchronous retry (bounded at 2 attempts).
• Pros: lower tail-latency for common cases, graceful degradation. Cons: added complexity (background retry + reconciliation).

Embeddings + reranker guidance:
• Bind candidate IDs to deterministic keys and store embeddings with model-version metadata. When model updates, keep previous embeddings for a rolling window and mark 'stale' for re-embedding asynchronously.
• Hot-path: use cached embeddings; cold-path: regenerate embeddings on first access with a cache-miss policy and rate-limit re-embeds to avoid spikes.

SDK integration notes (what I’ll demo):
• Pre-send hook: schema sanitizer that drops unexpected keys and coerces types where safe.
• Post-response hook: validator that returns structured error codes (VALIDATION_OK, INVALID_ENUM, TYPE_MISMATCH).
• Retry helper: small client lib call that runs the bounded synchronous retry loop when validators flag critical failures.

I’ll prepare a 30-min demo on Tuesday that includes: a short live run showing a bad enum being corrected via retry, and the SDK hooks in a sample Node client.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

message_4_subject: Re: Post-demo: response robustness playbook & decode-resilience next steps — proposed patterns
message_4_body:
Thanks Dev — that is helpful. A couple of pragmatic asks before the demo: 

• Can you include a brief run-through of the Node SDK pre/post hooks and where to plug a custom validator?
• For the embeddings plan: how do you track approximate staleness for business metrics (we want to avoid sudden ranking regressions during a model rollout)?

Also, we prefer Pattern B (soft-validate + retry) for now but need a clear metric to signal when to flip to Pattern A for a particular route (e.g., >X% validation failures over a 24h window). If you can show how we signal that in the console (per-route error rates), that would be great.

— Priya
Priya Shah
Product Manager, FinLytics
